=={{header|FreeBASIC}}==
{{trans|Wren}}
{{libheader|FreeImage}}
FreeBASIC lacks native or (to my knowledge) third-party support for face detection. Therefore, much like Wren's solution, we turn to an external utility for this task: facedetect, a free, easy-to-use tool available directly in the Ubuntu repositories.
<syntaxhighlight lang="vbnet">#include once "FreeImage.bi"

' Structure for bounding boxes
Type FaceBox
    x As Integer
    y As Integer
    w As Integer
    h As Integer
End Type

Function RunCommand(cmd As String) As String
    Dim f As FILE Ptr = popen(cmd, "r")
    If f = 0 Then Return ""
    
    Dim buffer As String = ""
    Dim chunk As ZString * 1024
    
    While fgets(@chunk, 1024, f) <> 0
        buffer &= chunk
    Wend
    
    pclose(f)
    Return buffer
End Function

Sub DrawBox(img As FIBITMAP Ptr, x As Integer, y As Integer, w As Integer, h As Integer)
    Dim As RGBQUAD col = (255, 255, 0, 0)
    
    For xx As Integer = x To x + w
        FreeImage_SetPixelColor(img, xx, y, @col)
        FreeImage_SetPixelColor(img, xx, y + h, @col)
    Next
    
    For yy As Integer = y To y + h
        FreeImage_SetPixelColor(img, x, yy, @col)
        FreeImage_SetPixelColor(img, x + w, yy, @col)
    Next
End Sub

Sub DrawAllBoxes(inFile As String, outFile As String, faces() As FaceBox)
    Dim As FIBITMAP Ptr img = FreeImage_Load(FIF_JPEG, inFile, JPEG_DEFAULT)
    If img = 0 Then
        Print "Error loading image "; inFile
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Get actual image height
    Dim As Integer w = FreeImage_GetWidth(img)
    Dim As Integer h = FreeImage_GetHeight(img)
    
    For i As Integer = 0 To Ubound(faces)
        Dim fx As Integer = faces(i).x
        Dim fy As Integer = faces(i).y
        Dim fw As Integer = faces(i).w
        Dim fh As Integer = faces(i).h

        ' Convert Top-Down -> Bottom-Up coordinate
        DrawBox(img, fx, h - fy - fh, fw, fh)
    Next
    
    FreeImage_Save(FIF_JPEG, img, outFile, JPEG_DEFAULT)
    FreeImage_Unload(img)
End Sub

' Main program
Const inFile  = "AOBABA176.jpg"
Const outFile = "fb_facedetection.jpg"

#ifdef __FB_LINUX__
    Dim result As String = RunCommand("facedetect -o " & outFile & " " & inFile)
#else
    ' The facedetect command-line tool is designed primarily for Unix/Linux 
    ' systems, but it can be used on Windows using Python with OpenCV.
    ' We run it on Windows from WSL:
    Dim result As String = RunCommand("wsl facedetect -o " & outFile & " " & inFile)
#endif 

If Len(result) = 0 Then Print "Error running facedetect": Sleep: End

Dim lines() As String
Dim cntLines As Integer = 0
Dim psc As Integer = 1
Dim nextPos As Integer

Do
    nextPos = Instr(psc, result, Chr(10))
    If nextPos = 0 Then Exit Do
    
    Redim Preserve lines(cntLines)
    lines(cntLines) = Trim(Mid(result, psc, nextPos - psc))
    cntLines += 1
    
    psc = nextPos + 1
Loop

Print cntLines; " faces detected on photo image '"; inFile; !"':\n"

' Parsear bounding boxes
Redim faces(cntLines - 1) As FaceBox

Dim i As Integer, j As Integer
Dim p() As String
For i = 0 To cntLines - 1
    Dim np As Integer = 0
    
    Dim s As String = lines(i)
    Dim t As String = ""
    
    For c As Integer = 1 To Len(s)
        Dim ch As String = Mid(s, c, 1)
        If ch = " " Then
            If Len(t) > 0 Then
                Redim Preserve p(np)
                p(np) = t
                np += 1
                t = ""
            End If
        Else
            t &= ch
        End If
    Next
    
    If Len(t) > 0 Then
        Redim Preserve p(np)
        p(np) = t
        np += 1
    End If
    
    If np = 4 Then
        faces(i).x = Val(p(0))
        faces(i).y = Val(p(1))
        faces(i).w = Val(p(2))
        faces(i).h = Val(p(3))
    End If
Next

' Sort the data by y-coord and print it to stdout.
For i = 0 To cntLines - 2
    For j = i + 1 To cntLines - 1
        If faces(j).y < faces(i).y Then Swap faces(i), faces(j)
    Next
Next

Print "x-coord   y-coord   width   height"
Print String(35, "-")

For i = 0 To cntLines - 1
    With faces(i)
        Print Using "  ####      ####    ####     ####"; .x; .y; .w; .h
    End With
Next
Print

' Extract and analyse y-coords.
Redim ys(cntLines - 1) As Double

For i = 0 To cntLines - 1
    ys(i) = faces(i).y
Next

Dim median As Double
If cntLines Mod 2 = 1 Then
    median = ys(cntLines \ 2)
Else
    median = (ys(cntLines \ 2 - 1) + ys(cntLines \ 2)) / 2
End If

Dim mean As Double = 0
For i = 0 To cntLines - 1
    mean += ys(i)
Next
mean /= cntLines

Dim stdDev As Double = 0
For i = 0 To cntLines - 1
    stdDev += (ys(i) - mean) ^ 2
Next
stdDev = Sqr(stdDev / cntLines)

Print Using "Median of y-coords = ###.##"; median
Print Using "Mean   of y-coords = ###.##"; mean
Print Using "StdDev of y-coords = ###.##"; stdDev
Print

' Check if there are any y-coords more than 1 s/d from both the median and the mean.
Print "The 'faces' with the following y-coordinates may be false positives:"
For i = 0 To cntLines - 1
    Dim dev1 As Double = Abs(ys(i) - median)
    Dim dev2 As Double = Abs(ys(i) - mean)
    If dev1 > stdDev And dev2 > stdDev Then Print ys(i)
Next

' Display bounded box image.
DrawAllBoxes(inFile, outFile, faces())
#ifdef __FB_LINUX__
    Dim cmdOpen As String = "xdg-open " & Chr(34) & outFile & Chr(34)
    ' Or
    ' Dim cmdOpen As String = "eog " & Chr(34) & outFile & Chr(34)
#else
    ' Opens the default image viewer:
    Dim cmdOpen As String = "cmd /c start """" """ & outFile & """"
#endif
Shell cmdOpen

Sleep</syntaxhighlight>
